scenes.headline: How Qwen-CUA works a computer from pixels alone
scenes.sub: Screenshots in, keyboard and mouse out, and a smarter way to forget.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Bluebell! Qwen-CUA runs a computer from screenshots alone, with keyboard and mouse. Here's the trick that makes long tasks affordable.

scenes.text: Fold old screenshots ten at a time, not one per turn, so the prefix holds still and the cache is reused.
scenes.say: The idea: fold old screenshots ten at a time, not one per turn. The prompt prefix holds still, so the cache can be reused.

steps.say: It sees only a screenshot. No page structure, no accessibility tree. The model is a three hundred ninety-seven billion parameter mixture of experts.
Each turn, it emits one action: a key, a click, a drag, a scroll, or a call to the user when it's stuck.
The new screenshot joins an active history of twenty. Past that, the oldest ten fold at once into a text placeholder. Their reasoning and actions stay.

left.title: Fold one per turn
left.say: Fold one screenshot per turn, and the prefix changes every turn. Every request looks new to the cache, and pays full prefill.

right.title: Fold ten at once
right.say: Fold ten at once, and steps twenty-one to thirty share one prefix, so cached keys and values get reused. Training folds the same way.

scenes.label: vCPUs in the rollout fleet, where a stable prefix saves prefill
scenes.note: tens of thousands of concurrent environments
scenes.say: That matters at scale. The rollout fleet has close to a hundred thousand virtual CPUs, and every stable prefix is prefill it doesn't redo.

scenes.label: Benchmarks Qwen-CUA leads outright
scenes.note: 86.2 on OSWorld-Verified, a benchmark XLang Lab built
scenes.say: The results: eighty-six point two on OSWorld-Verified, a benchmark co-author XLang Lab built. It leads two of eight benchmarks outright, and trails on safety.

scenes.text: The new part is systems: fold history in blocks, and a huge rollout fleet stops recomputing prefixes it already has.

scenes.say: To recap: pixels in, one action out, and history folded in blocks so the cache stays warm.
